title: Accounts & Payroll Administrator
company: Hays Accounts and Finance - Agency - Permanent
description:
Accounts & Payroll Administrator
Part-Time 3 Days per Week
Your New CompanyHays Accountancy & Finance is recruiting on behalf of an established organisation for an experienced Accounts & Payroll Administrator to join their finance function on a part-time basis. This is a varied position offering exposure across transactional finance, payroll, reconciliations and month-end support.The role would suit someone looking for a three-day working week who enjoys taking ownership of day-to-day finance processes within a busy working environment.
Your New RoleAs Accounts & Payroll Administrator, you will play an important role in supporting the smooth running of the organisation's finance and payroll activities.Your responsibilities will include:
- Managing accounts payable and accounts receivable processes
- Handling supplier and customer account queries
- Supporting credit control and following up outstanding balances
- Preparing payment runs and maintaining accurate transaction records
- Posting banking activity and completing bank reconciliations
- Reconciling cash, balance sheet and other control accounts
- Maintaining accurate accounting records and ensuring appropriate VAT treatment
- Assisting with month-end management accounts, including accruals and prepayments
- Investigating financial discrepancies and escalating issues where appropriate
- Processing employee payroll accurately and within required deadlines
- Maintaining payroll records for new starters, leavers and employee changes
- Reviewing payroll information and resolving discrepancies
- Producing payroll reports to support management and audit requirements
- Maintaining accurate records and supporting compliance with relevant payroll requirements

What You'll Need to SucceedYou will ideally have previous experience in an Accounts Administrator, Finance Assistant, Payroll Administrator or similar finance role, with practical knowledge of both bookkeeping and payroll processes.You should have:
- Previous experience within accounts and/or payroll
- Good understanding of bookkeeping and transactional finance processes
- Experience using accounting and payroll software
- Experience with Xero would be highly advantageous
- Good working knowledge of Microsoft Excel
- Strong reconciliation and numerical skills
- High levels of accuracy and attention to detail
- Good organisational and record-keeping skills
- Confident written and verbal communication skills

An AAT/Accounting Technician qualification or similar would be desirable but is not essential where you can demonstrate relevant practical experience.
What You'll Get in ReturnYou will have the opportunity to join an established organisation in a varied position offering exposure across both accounts and payroll. The role is offered on a part-time, three-day-per-week basis, making it particularly attractive to candidates seeking greater flexibility while continuing to develop broad finance experience.You'll work across several areas of the finance function rather than being restricted to one transactional discipline, giving you the opportunity to utilise and develop your experience across accounts, payroll, reconciliations and month-end processes.

title: Bookkeeper
description:
Bookkeeper (Fixed-Term Contract with Permanent Opportunity)

Salary: £28,000 - £30,000 per annum (depending on experience)
Contract: Initial 3-Month Fixed-Term Contract with potential to become permanent
Hours: Full-time preferred. Part-time (minimum 30 hours per week) will be considered for the right candidate.

About the Role

We are currently seeking an organised and detail-oriented Bookkeeper to join our finance team on an initial three-month fixed-term contract. This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced finance professional looking to join a supportive and growing business, with a strong possibility of the role becoming permanent.
Working as part of a small finance team, you will play a key role in supporting the Senior Management Team through the accurate and timely processing of financial transactions, maintaining sales and purchase ledgers, bank reconciliations, credit control activities, and providing wider administrative support.

Key Responsibilities
- Maintain accurate Purchase and Sales Ledger records.
- Process purchase invoices and match them to purchase orders.
- Reconcile customer accounts and sales ledger transactions.
- Perform multi-currency bank reconciliations and ensure correct allocation of transactions.
- Support the credit control function, helping to ensure timely customer payments.
- Respond to customer queries regarding invoices and payments.
- Assist with the cleansing and maintenance of supplier and customer records.
- Provide general administrative support to Senior Management and the wider business.
- Contribute to continuous improvement initiatives within the finance function.
- Undertake any other reasonable duties as required by management.

Essential Criteria
- Minimum of 5 GCSEs (or equivalent), including Maths and English.
- At least 2 years' experience in a bookkeeping, accounts, finance, or administration role.
- Strong Microsoft Office skills, particularly Excel.
- Excellent numerical, analytical, and data-entry skills with a high level of accuracy.
- Ability to manage workloads effectively and meet deadlines.
- Strong organisational and multitasking skills.
- Excellent communication skills and a professional telephone manner.
- Experience using finance, accounting, or ERP systems.

Desirable Criteria
- Accounting Technician qualification, or currently studying towards an accounting qualification.
- Experience using Sage, particularly Sage Intacct.
- Experience using Opera accounting software.
- Previous experience working within a busy finance department.

Skills & Attributes

The successful candidate will demonstrate:
Attention to Detail
A commitment to accuracy and maintaining high-quality financial records.
Communication Skills
The ability to build positive relationships with customers, suppliers, and colleagues.
Organisation & Time Management
The ability to prioritise workloads effectively while meeting deadlines.
Team Player
A flexible and collaborative approach, with a willingness to support colleagues and contribute to the success of the wider business.

What's on Offer?
- Competitive salary- depending on experience.
- Opportunity to secure a permanent position following the initial contract period.
- Flexible working options, with part-time hours considered.
- Supportive and friendly team environment.
- Career development opportunities within a growing business.

If you are an experienced Bookkeeper looking for your next opportunity and want to join a company where your contribution will be valued, we'd love to hear from you.

Brook Street NMR is acting as an Employment Agency in relation to this vacancy.

company: Hays Accounts and Finance - Agency - Permanent
description:
Property Management Finance AssistantLocation: Belfast Job Type: Permanent Full-time Working Pattern: Office-based Hours: Monday to Friday
Your New CompanyHays Accountancy & Finance is delighted to be working with an established and successful organisation in the property sector to recruit a Property Management Finance Assistant.This is an excellent opportunity to join a growing business where you will become an important part of a close-knit finance function. You will work alongside the senior finance team and have responsibility for ensuring accurate day-to-day financial processing across the business.
Your New RoleAs Property Management Finance Assistant, you will take responsibility for a broad range of transactional finance and bookkeeping duties, ensuring financial information is accurate, reconciled and maintained to a high standard.Your key responsibilities will include:
- Processing purchase invoices, sales invoices, receipts and payments
- Completing regular bank reconciliations and investigating outstanding items
- Managing the purchase ledger, including supplier invoices, statement reconciliations and preparing payment runs
- Managing the sales ledger, including raising invoices, allocating receipts and following up on outstanding balances
- Maintaining accurate aged creditor and debtor reports
- Coding financial transactions accurately using accounting software
- Supporting the finance team with intercompany transactions and reconciliations
- Assisting the wider property management team with rent-related transactions, payments and financial administration
- Supporting the reconciliation of client accounts and ensuring accurate financial records are maintained
- Working closely with colleagues across the business to resolve finance-related queries
- Providing additional support to the finance function during month-end reporting

What You'll Need to SucceedTo be successful in this position, you should have:
- At least 2 years' experience within a finance, bookkeeping, property management or similar environment
- Previous experience across purchase ledger, sales ledger and bank reconciliations
- Good working knowledge of cloud-based accounting software
- Strong Microsoft Excel skills
- Excellent numerical accuracy and attention to detail
- The ability to manage multiple deadlines and priorities
- Strong organisational skills with a proactive approach to your work
- The confidence to communicate financial information to non-finance colleagues
- A professional and discreet approach when handling confidential information

Previous experience within the property or estate agency sector would be particularly advantageous but is not essential for candidates with strong transactional finance experience.
What You'll Get in ReturnIn return, you will receive:
- Competitive salary, reviewed annually
- 25 days' annual leave plus bank holidays
- Workplace pension
- Permanent, full-time employment
- Monday-to-Friday working hours
- The opportunity to develop broad transactional finance experience
- Exposure to a varied role covering purchase ledger, sales ledger, reconciliations and wider finance
- The chance to join an established organisation and work closely with an experienced finance team

If you're interested in this role, click 'apply now' to forward an up-to-date copy of your CV, or contact Hays Accountancy & Finance for a confidential discussion about your career.

title: Finance Assistant
description:
Main purpose of job Finance Assistant

To be responsible to the Finance Officer (Cashier Service) for the delivery of a quality cashier service.

To assist with managing the councils cash resources and bank accounts in line with the needs of user departments.

Summary of responsibilities and personal duties Finance Assistant
- To assist the Finance Officer (Cashier Service) with tasks relating to the management of the cashier service including its bank accounts.
- To assist the Finance Officer (Cashier Service) with the updating of appropriate policies, regulations and legislation.
- To provide advice and guidance to user departments and suppliers with regard to the cashier service.
- To liaise with the appropriate bank(s) under the direction of the Finance Officer (Cashier Service) with regard to banking facilities and queries.
- To administer payroll deductions and ensure timely payment to recipients, for example, Inland Revenue, NILGOSC, Trade Unions and other relevant bodies.
- To process payments in relation to Accounts Payable and Payroll transactions.
- To assist with the administration and preparation of statistical reports relating to the Cashiers Imprest Bank Account, Euro Bank Account and other bank accounts relevant to the cashier service.
- To assist the Finance Officer (Cashier Service) with maintaining, updating and monitoring a list of the councils bank accounts.
- To assist with the Bankers Automatic Clearing Systems (BACS) on behalf of the council by liaising with the sponsor, BACS and Digital Services in respect of new developments.
- To assist with the implementation of best value and quality improvements.
- To make recommendations to the Finance Officer (Cashier Service) with regard to developing and improving the service.
- To participate in all induction and in-service training provided by Belfast City Council and in the induction and support of all newly appointed staff and other human resource management policies and procedures, as appropriate, including, absence management, disciplinary and grievance procedure.
- To act in accordance with the council and departmental policies and procedures including customer care, equal opportunities, health and safety, safeguarding and any pertinent legislation.
- To undertake the duties in such a way as to enhance and protect the reputation and public profile of the council.
- To undertake such other relevant duties as may from time to time be required.

Experience Finance Assistant

Applicants must, as at the closing date for receipt of application forms, be able to demonstrate, by providing personal and specific examples on the application form, at least one years relevant experience in each of the following areas:
- working in a financial environment and dealing with reconciliation of payments in 1 a large public or private sector organisation;
- using Microsoft Office IT applications and financial packages used for the processing of BACS payments; and
- working in a busy office environment as part of a team, using prioritisation skills to adhere to strict deadlines.

title: Finance Administrator
description:
Finance Administrator
- Location: Larne Area
- Contract: Full-time Permanent Office-based
- Salary: £28,000 - £30,000 per annum

Reed is partnered with a world leading business in the Larne area in the appointment of an experienced Finance Administrator on a permanent & full-time basis. The successful Finance Administrator will support the efficient running of Accounts Payable and Finance Administration areas.

This role involves managing accounts payable, finance administration, and occasionally assisting with visitor and contractor management on-site. Reporting to the Office Supervisor, this position is crucial for maintaining smooth operations between the business and suppliers/vendors.

Day-to-day of the role:
- Invoice Processing: Review, verify, and process supplier invoices using SAP, ensure all invoices are correctly coded to appropriate general ledger accounts and cost centres and match invoices to purchase orders and goods receipts
- Vendor Management: Maintain accurate and complete vendor master data in SAP, respond to supplier queries promptly and professionally & reconcile vendor statements and resolve discrepancies.
- Travel & Expenses: Audit travel and expense submissions as guided by the Office Supervisor.
- Payments: Ensure timely reconciliation and transaction of cash postings.
- Reconciliations & Reporting: Perform regular accounts payable reconciliations, assist with month-end closing activities, and support audits by providing necessary documentation and explanations.

Required Skills & Qualifications:
- Proven experience in an accounts payable role with a strong understanding of end-to-end processes.
- Preferable experience with SAP as an ERP system.
- Ability to handle confidential material and associated issues professionally.
- Proficiency in Microsoft applications (Excel & Word).

For more information, including package details, please contact Mary at Reed Belfast, apply via this advert, or contact me confidentially on LinkedIn

description:
Finance AdministratorLocation: Larne Full-time Permanent
Your New CompanyHays is delighted to be working with an established and successful organisation in the Larne area to recruit a Finance Administrator to join their finance team.This is an excellent opportunity for someone with Accounts Payable or broader finance administration experience who is looking to develop their career within a professional and well-structured finance environment.
